name: Jehudi
title: The King's Messenger
summary: Jehudi was a court official who served under King Jehoiakim of Judah. He is best known for reading the scroll of the prophet Jeremiah aloud to the king, and for being the messenger sent to fetch Baruch with the scroll to the princes. When he read the scroll before the king, Jehoiakim cut it into pieces and threw it into the fire.

keyEvents.title: Jehudi's lineage is mentioned
keyEvents.description: Jehudi's ancestry is described: he was the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, showing that he came from a well-known family at court.

keyEvents.title: Sent to fetch Baruch
keyEvents.description: The princes sent Jehudi to fetch Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, who had the scroll containing the prophet's words, so they could hear its contents.

keyEvents.title: Baruch reads the scroll to the princes
keyEvents.description: After Jehudi fetched Baruch, he read the scroll aloud to the princes, and they were struck with fear at the message.

keyEvents.title: Jehudi reads the scroll for King Jehoiakim
keyEvents.description: Jehudi was asked to read Jeremiah's scroll aloud to King Jehoiakim, who was sitting in his winter house by the fire. Jehudi read column after column for the king.

keyEvents.title: King Jehoiakim burns the scroll
keyEvents.description: As Jehudi read three or four columns at a time, King Jehoiakim cut them off with a scribe's knife and threw them into the fire, until the entire scroll was burned up, despite protests from some of the princes.

keyEvents.title: God's judgment on Jehoiakim
keyEvents.description: After the scroll was burned, the Lord commanded Jeremiah to write a new scroll containing all the original words, plus additional words of judgment against King Jehoiakim for his defiant act.
